text:
Liam: heads up — canary shows a ~25-40ms p95 regression on SSE streaming after last night's release. Visible even at low QPS.
Anya: yikes. only streaming or other endpoints too?
Liam: streaming chat + tool-calls path. non-streaming gen fine.
Matt: perf-ci opened an alert: streaming_slo_end_to_first_byte p95 +28.4ms vs baseline.
perf-ci: [alert] job=perf-suite/streaming_slo_end_to_first_byte run=11234 delta=+28.4ms threshold=+15ms url=https://perf.ci/runs/11234
Liam: quick flame summary from canary agent (condensed):
```
flamegraph summary:
  34%  runtime:serialize_tool_payload
  22%  sse/flush_coalescer
  18%  kernel_selector::choose_kernel
  10%  kv_cache::lookup (misses ++ after merge)
```
Anya: serialize_tool_payload? PR#2345 changed the tool envelope to a unified protobuf before SSE. That was supposed to be a protocol-only change.
Matt: yes — we now protobuf::encode the whole envelope before calling the SSE writer. before we streamed frames raw. quick local repro:
```
// before
sse_writer.write_chunk(raw_chunk)
// after
let payload = protobuf::encode(&ToolEnvelope { .. })?; // blocking encode
sse_writer.write_chunk(payload)
```
Anya: protobuf::encode is sync and does an allocation + copy. for large tool metadata that can add 10-30ms on the request path.
Liam: KV hit-rate dropped ~6% on canary too. hypothesis: packing metadata into one envelope changes prefix boundaries used by our prefix KV cache -> more churn.
Matt: traces show kv_cache lookup often happens after serialization in the new code path, which increases in-flight time and hurts batching and kernel choice. we also see sse flush coalescer waiting longer.
Anya: bisect time. i'll git-bisect the release branch now (starting at 1756a...). will report commit.
perf-ci: [ci] perf-suite/streaming_end_to_first_byte started run=11235
Anya: bisect found the culprit: commit 9c7d2b2 (PR #2345) — moving tool envelope encode to before SSE writer.
Matt: quick mitigation idea: move encode responsibility into the SSE writer and stream-encode (incremental encode) instead of a big blocking encode. i sketched a patch.
Liam: canary rollout paused by the deploy guard due to perf thresholds.
deploy-bot: [rollout] canary paused at 30% (auto-paused by perf SLO guard)
Matt: patch excerpt (concept):
```
- let payload = protobuf::encode(&env)?;
- sse_writer.write_chunk(payload);
+ sse_writer.start_envelope();
+ protobuf::stream_encode(&env, |chunk| sse_writer.write_chunk(chunk));
+ sse_writer.finish_envelope();
```
Anya: streaming encoder amortizes work and doesn't block the writer thread. also reduces the window where kv lookups see a different execution order.
Liam: ran a local canary with the streaming-encode hotfix — perf-suite run shows p95 delta +0.5ms (baselines are within noise). kv hit-rate recovered.
perf-ci: run=11235 result: streaming_slo_end_to_first_byte p95 delta=+0.5ms
Liam: plan: 1) open a revert/hotfix PR reverting the placement in the release branch 2) add streaming-encode utility and unit + microbench tests 3) CI perf test for serialization blocking/active-serialization-time.
Anya: also add a canary gate for serialization-blocking increases >10ms and a kv-cache-stability check.
Sre-oncall: adding a follow-up pager rule in case canary still fails after revert.
Liam: i'll open the revert PR + the streaming encode PR and attach perf traces + kv graphs.
Matt: once revert merges we'll resume rollout and run extended perf-suite.
Anya: note to self/team: protocol-only changes can change execution ordering and surface in perf-critical code paths. always run a small serialization microbench when touching protocol envelopes.
Liam: tagging @eng-runtime and @eng-releases for visibility. :thumbsup:
